faqs.a: Borders meet at 45-degree angles. When an element has zero width and height, its four borders become four triangles meeting at the centre. Colouring one border and making the rest transparent leaves a single triangle.

keyFacts: CSS triangles use the border trick: zero-size box, one coloured border, rest transparent.
Up triangle: transparent left/right borders, coloured bottom border.
Side border widths equal half the triangle width (50px for a 100px wide triangle).
The coloured border's width equals the triangle height.
The triangle points away from the coloured border.
Works in every browser - it is plain CSS with no dependencies.

limitations: Only right-style border triangles - no curved or gradient triangles.
Hex colours only in the picker; convert rgba yourself after pasting.
Very large triangles (near 400px) can look jagged on some screens.
The trick needs a zero-size element, so it cannot wrap text inside.
